lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Know it, prepare for it, and help each other. Today, we follow the light of the Safety Lantern to the small airport on the Island of Fire. Look at its big white roof. It looks like two huge wings! That's why people call it the Airport of Wings. Birimo opens his map. There's a little wings mark right here! Then a young albatross comes over to us. She wears a blue scarf and a captain's cap. Hello! I'm Skye, the junior guide of this airport. Every trip is a story! She points to the tall windows. Planes are taking off one after another. Skye says, From here, planes leave for every corner of the world. Say it with me. Planes leave for every corner of the world. Great! I smile and hold up my travel pouch. Your passports are safe in here, I say. We're going on a trip abroad together! Skye gives each of us a small blue book. Let's read the first page. "Welcome to the Wing Stamp Book! This is not a passport. It is a book for your travel story. There are six empty pages inside. Each time you finish one part of your trip, one page will be filled. Use polite words, help your friends, and always stay with your group. When all six pages are full, a big surprise is waiting for you. Have a wonderful trip, and remember, every trip is a story!" How many empty pages are there? Six. Is the Wing Stamp Book a passport? No, it isn't. It's a book for our travel story. Now, phonics. Look at the departures board. We read flight numbers in small parts. Flight 205 is flight two oh five. Zero often sounds like oh. Flight 318 is flight three eighteen. Flight 760 is flight seven sixty. Flight 1120 is flight eleven twenty. Our plane is Flight 205! Next time, we will go to the check-in counter with our bags!

vocab.ja: チェックイン カウンター

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Planes leave for every corner of the world. Today, we pull our suitcases to the check-in counter. There's a short line, so we wait our turn. Then a friendly clerk in a green jacket waves to us. I step up to the counter with all of you and say, Good morning. I'd like to check in, please. Say it with me. I'd like to check in, please. Great! Before we go on, let's read the sign on the counter. "Welcome to the Check-In Counter. Check-in for Flight 205 opens at 7:15 and closes at 10:00. Please have your passport ready. Put your bags on the scale one at a time. We will put a baggage tag on each bag, so it can find its way to the right plane. Keep medicine and important things in your small bag. After check-in, please go to the security check. Have a wonderful flight!" What time does check-in open? At 7:15. What goes on each bag? A baggage tag. The clerk asks, May I see your passports, please? I take our passports out of my travel pouch. Here you are. Then the clerk asks, How many bags are you checking? Two bags, please. The bags go on the scale, and the clerk puts a baggage tag on each one. Bye-bye, bags! See you later! Birimo tries to climb onto the scale, too. Oh, Birimo! You're not a bag! Everyone laughs, even the clerk. Now, phonics. Let's read times. Say the hour, and then the minutes. 10:45 is ten forty-five. That's when our plane leaves. 6:05 is six oh five. The zero sounds like oh. 12:30 is twelve thirty. 7:15 is seven fifteen. Listen carefully. Fifteen is strong at the end. Fifty is strong at the beginning. Next time, we will choose our seats. Do you like the window or the aisle?

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I'd like to check in, please. We are still at the check-in counter. Our bags have their tags, and now it's time to choose our seats. The clerk looks at Haru and asks, Would you like a window seat or an aisle seat? Say it with me. Would you like a window seat or an aisle seat? Great! An aisle is the long, narrow path between the seats. Haru doesn't need to think. A window seat, please! I want to see the clouds. Sure. Your seat is 14A. Kiko says, I'd like an aisle seat, please. Then I can stand up and stretch my legs. Riko is happy in the middle, between her two friends. I ask, Can we sit together? The clerk smiles. Of course. You're all in rows 14 and 15. I'll sit right behind Haru, Riko, and Kiko, in 15B. Then the clerk prints our boarding passes. Let's read Haru's boarding pass. "Boarding Pass. Passenger: Haru. Flight: 205. From: the Airport of Wings. To: Skyport International Airport. Gate: 23B. Boarding time: 10:15. Departure time: 10:45. Seat: 14A, window. Seats A and F are next to the windows. Please be at your gate by boarding time. The gate closes fifteen minutes before departure. Keep this boarding pass with your passport until you are on the plane. Thank you, and enjoy your flight!" What is Haru's seat? 14A, a window seat. What time does boarding start? At 10:15. Birimo reads his boarding pass. Seat 15A! A window seat, too! He does a happy little dance. Now, phonics. Seat numbers are a number and a letter. Seat 14A is seat fourteen A. Seat 32F is seat thirty-two F. Seat 8C is seat eight C. Seat 21D is seat twenty-one D. Be careful with fourteen and forty. Fourteen is strong at the end. Forty is strong at the beginning. Next time, we will listen to the airport announcements very carefully!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Would you like a window seat or an aisle seat? Today, we go through the security check. We put our small bags on the belt, and they ride slowly through a big machine. Then we walk through a gate, one by one, and I watch everyone go through. Beep! Oh, it's just Birimo's empty metal water bottle. A staff member checks it, smiles, and gives it back. No problem! After security, we sit in the waiting area by the big windows. Skye says, Airports are full of announcements, so listen carefully for your flight number. Let's read the announcements we heard this morning. "Good morning, passengers. Flight 318 to Sunny Bay is now boarding at gate 41C. Passengers on Flight 760 to Pine Island, your gate has changed. Please go to gate 15. Passengers on Flight 205 to Skyport International Airport, please have your boarding pass and passport ready. Families with small children may board first. Flight 205 leaves at 10:45. Thank you for waiting." Where is Flight 318 boarding? At gate 41C. Who may board Flight 205 first? Families with small children. Then a bell rings. Ding-dong! Flight 205 is now boarding at gate 23B. That's us! Say it with me. Flight 205 is now boarding at gate 23B. Great! Boarding means getting on the plane. Haru jumps up. Did you hear that? Riko nods. Yes! That's our flight! I say, Let's get our things. Stay close to me, everyone. Now, phonics. Gate numbers are like seat numbers. Gate 23B is gate twenty-three B. Gate 41C is gate forty-one C. Gate 102 is gate one oh two. The zero sounds like oh. Gate 15 is gate fifteen. Fifteen is strong at the end, so don't mix it up with fifty. Next time, we will look for gate 23B and say goodbye to Skye!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Flight 205 is now boarding at gate 23B. We pick up our bags and walk down the long hall. But wait. There are two signs. One arrow says Gates 1 to 20. The other arrow says Gates 21 to 30, but it points up! Where is gate 23B? I see an airport staff member in a yellow vest. We all go over together, and Riko asks politely. Excuse me. Do you know where gate 23B is? Say it with me. Excuse me. Do you know where gate 23B is? Great! It's a softer way to say, Where is gate 23B? The staff member smiles. Yes! Go up the stairs and turn left. It's next to the big window. Riko says, Thank you so much! At gate 23B, Skye is waiting for us. She opens our Wing Stamp Books and presses a little stamp on the first page. Let's read the note she wrote next to it. "Dear friends, today you checked in, chose your seats, listened to the announcements, and asked the way politely. You did a wonderful job! Here is your first stamp, a little blue plane. On the plane, fasten your seatbelts and stay close to Ms. Emma. I'm going to fly across the sea, too, so I'll see you again soon. Every trip is a story, and yours is just beginning! Love, Skye" What is the first stamp? A little blue plane. What will Skye do? She'll fly across the sea and see us again. Goodbye, Skye! She waves her long wings. Have a great flight! I'll fly to meet you! Now, phonics. Let's review our airport numbers. Flight 205 is flight two oh five. 10:45 is ten forty-five. Seat 14A is seat fourteen A. Gate 23B is gate twenty-three B. Next time, we will be on the plane, high above the clouds!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Excuse me. Do you know where gate 23B is? Today, we are on Flight 205! Haru sits by the window in 14A, Riko is in 14B, and Kiko is on the aisle in 14C. Birimo and I are right behind them. Ding! The seatbelt sign is on, so we fasten our seatbelts. Click! The plane goes faster and faster down the runway, and then we're in the air! Haru's ears feel strange. I say, Try yawning or chewing. That helps. Soon a kind flight attendant comes down the aisle with a cart. Kiko is thirsty, so she asks, Could I have some water, please? Say it with me. Could I have some water, please? Great! The flight attendant smiles. Of course. Here you are. Riko feels a little cold. Could I have a blanket, please? Then the pilot makes an announcement. Let's read it. "Hello, everyone. This is your captain speaking. Welcome aboard Flight 205. We are now flying high above the sea. The weather is clear, and the visibility is excellent, so please look out your window. You can see small green islands below. In a few minutes, our flight attendants will serve a light lunch. When the seatbelt sign is on, please stay in your seat with your seatbelt fastened. Thank you, and enjoy the flight!" What can we see out the window? Small green islands. What will the flight attendants serve? A light lunch. Now, phonics. Vis means see. Vision means how well you can see. Birds like Skye have amazing vision. Visibility means how far you can see. On a foggy day, the visibility is poor. Visual means about seeing. The safety card is very visual. It has pictures, so you can understand it with your eyes. Next time, we will land in a new country and meet a passport officer!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Could I have some water, please? After a long flight, we land at Skyport International Airport. It's huge! There are moving walkways, bright signs, and travelers from all over the world. I say, Stay together, everyone. First, we go to passport control. Let's read the sign on the wall. "Welcome to Skyport International Airport. All visitors, please go to Passport Control. Have your passport ready. Families may go to the officer together, and children should stay with their adult. The officer will check your passport and may ask you a few simple questions, for example, why you are visiting and how long you will stay. After that, collect your bags and go through Customs. Enjoy your stay!" What should children do? Stay with their adult. Where do you go after passport control? To Customs. Now it's our turn. We walk up to the desk together. A friendly officer smiles at us. Hello! What's the purpose of your visit? I answer, Sightseeing. Say it with me. What's the purpose of your visit? Sightseeing. Great! Purpose means reason. Sightseeing means visiting famous and beautiful places. The officer asks, How long will you stay? For five days. Where are you staying? At the Seagull Hotel in Brightwater. Then the officer looks at Kiko and asks, Is this your first visit? Kiko answers, Yes, it is! The officer laughs and says, Welcome! Have a wonderful time! Now, phonics. Vis means see. Visit means to go and see a person or a place. A visitor is a person who comes to see a place. A visa is a paper or stamp that lets you enter a country. Some countries need a visa, and some don't. I checked everything before our trip. Next time, we will look for our next plane to Brightwater!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, What's the purpose of your visit? Sightseeing. We are in a new country now, but our trip isn't over yet. Brightwater is a city by the sea, far from here, so we need to take one more plane. This is called a connecting flight. Our next plane is a domestic flight. Domestic means inside the same country. But Skyport is so big! We all walk to the transfer desk, and I ask, How do I transfer to my next flight? Say it with me. How do I transfer to my next flight? Great! The man at the desk smiles. Follow the green Connecting Flights signs, and check the departures board for your gate. Let's read the departures board. "Departures. Flight 1120 to Brightwater leaves at 4:20 from gate 41C. It is on time. Flight 760 to Green Valley leaves at 4:50 from gate 15. It is delayed. Flight 540 to Maple Hill leaves at 5:10 from gate 12. It is on time. Passengers with connecting flights, please follow the green signs. Your gate may change, so please check this board again before you go. If you need help, ask at the transfer desk next to the escalators." When does Flight 1120 leave? At 4:20. What should you do before you go to your gate? Check the board again. We follow the green signs. Haru reads every one out loud. Connecting Flights, this way! Birimo marches like a leader, but he stays right next to me. Now, phonics. Vis means see. Television. Tele means far, so a television shows pictures from far away. The departures board is on a big screen like a television. Invisible. In means not, so invisible means impossible to see. Supervise. Super means over. I supervise you. I watch over you and keep you safe. Next time, we will change some money while we wait for our plane!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, How do I transfer to my next flight? Our plane to Brightwater leaves at 4:20, so we have some time. I say, In this country, people use dollars, not yen. Different countries use different money. Let's go to the currency exchange counter. A friendly clerk says, Hello! How can I help you? I answer, I'd like to change some yen, please. Say it with me. I'd like to change some yen, please. Great! Before the clerk starts, let's read the sign on the counter. "Currency Exchange. Welcome to Skyport! Here, you can change your money into dollars. Today's exchange rate is on the board above the counter. The rate is a little different every day. Please count your money carefully before you leave the counter, and keep your receipt. If you need small coins for buses or snacks, just ask. Thank you, and have a great stay!" Where is today's exchange rate? On the board above the counter. What should you do before you leave? Count your money carefully. The clerk gives me some bills. I ask, Could we have some coins, too? Certainly. Here you are. Then I say, Let's count it together. Haru counts the bills. Ten, twenty, thirty dollars! Kiko counts the shiny coins. Birimo holds a coin up to the light. It has a seagull on it! I put the money in my pouch and zip it up. Now, phonics. Vis means see. Revise. Re means again. When you revise, you look at your work again and make it better. Riko revises her travel list. Advise means to tell someone what you think they should do. The clerk advises us to count carefully. A supervisor is a person who watches and guides other workers. Next time, we will finally arrive in Brightwater, and it's a very special lesson!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I'd like to change some yen, please. Today is a very special day. Flight 1120 flies over green hills and a sparkling blue sea. The pilot says, We will land in Brightwater in a few minutes. Haru looks out the window. He can see a tall Clock Tower, a river full of little boats, and an old castle on a hill. Bump! The plane lands at 6:05 in the evening. We walk out to the arrivals gate together, and guess who's waiting there? Skye! She's holding a big golden balloon with the number 1,000 on it. She flew all the way across the sea to meet us! Haru shouts, We've arrived! This is our 1,000th lesson! Say it with me. We've arrived! This is our 1,000th lesson! Wonderful! Skye gives us a card. Let's read it. "Dear Haru, Riko, Kiko, Birimo, and Ms. Emma, congratulations on your 1,000th lesson! You flew across the sea, answered the officer politely, found your connecting flight, and changed money like real travelers. Welcome to Brightwater, a sunny city by the sea. Here you can see the Clock Tower, ride a boat on the river, and walk up to the old castle on the hill. Please open your Wing Stamp Books. Every trip is a story! Love, Skye" What can you ride on the river? A boat. Where is the old castle? On the hill. Skye presses the second stamp into our books. It's a golden balloon! I say, One thousand lessons! I'm so proud of you all. Now, phonics. Let's review. Visit. Vis means see, so visit means to go and see a place. Visa. A visa is a paper or stamp that lets you enter a country. Flight 1120 is flight eleven twenty. And 6:05 is six oh five. Next time, we will check in at the Seagull Hotel!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, We've arrived! This is our 1,000th lesson! Now it's evening in Brightwater. Skye waves goodbye and flies off to visit a friend by the harbor. Then we walk to our hotel near the sea. It's called the Seagull Hotel, and a big wooden seagull hangs above the door. Inside, the lobby smells like fresh flowers. A man in a green jacket smiles at us from the front desk. His name is Mr. Lee, and he is always smiling. Before the trip, I made our reservation, and I put it under Haru's name. So Haru steps up to the desk with me and says, Good evening. I have a reservation under the name Haru. Say it with me. I have a reservation under the name Haru. Great! Mr. Lee checks his computer and says, Yes, here it is! Five guests, one adult and four children. Then he gives us a welcome card. Let's read the welcome card. "Welcome to the Seagull Hotel! Your room is 512 on the fifth floor. Breakfast is from seven to ten in the Harbor Room on the first floor. Check-out time is eleven in the morning. Please take your room key with you when you go out. If you need anything, call the front desk any time, day or night. We hope you enjoy your stay in Brightwater!" What is our room number? 512. When is breakfast? From seven to ten. Birimo wants to guard the key all night, but I keep it safe in my pouch. Now, phonics. Today's words have double letters, but we say the sound only once. Accommodation means a place to stay. It has two c's and two m's. Address has two d's and two s's. Necessary has one c and two s's. Next time, we will go up to our room and ask for things very politely!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I have a reservation under the name Haru. Today, we are in Room 512. It has two big beds and a window over a busy street. The room feels a little warm and stuffy. I'm unpacking my backpack. I turn to Haru and say, Would you mind opening the window? Haru says, Not at all! He opens it, and fresh sea air comes in. Would you mind（～して もらえますか）is a very polite way to ask someone to do something. After would you mind, we use an ing word: opening, closing, helping. Here is the funny part. Mind means feel bothered. So when you are happy to help, you say, Not at all! It means, It's no trouble at all. Say it with me. Would you mind opening the window? Wonderful! Let's read the room guide on the desk. "Room Guide. Coffee and tea are free. You can find them next to the kettle. Extra pillows and blankets are in the closet. If you need more towels, please call the front desk. Please close the window when you leave the room, and turn off the lights to save energy. Quiet time starts at ten at night. Thank you for being a kind guest!" Where are the extra pillows? In the closet. When does quiet time start? At ten at night. Kiko opens the closet, but there is only one extra pillow, and Birimo is already hugging it. Kiko smiles and asks, Birimo, would you mind sharing? Birimo says, Not at all! Now, phonics. More double letters today. Pillow has two l's. P, i, l, l, o, w. Coffee has two f's and two e's. C, o, f, f, e, e. Occupied means someone is using it, like a seat or a bathroom. It has two c's and one p. Next time, we will ask Mr. Lee how to get to the nearest station!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Would you mind opening the window? This morning, after a big breakfast in the Harbor Room, we want to explore Brightwater. I say the train is the easiest way. But where is the station? I say, Let's ask at the front desk. We walk to the lobby together. We could just ask, Where is the station? That's fine, but there is a softer, more polite way. Listen. Where is the station? becomes, Do you know where the station is? The verb is moves to the end. Where are the boats? becomes, Do you know where the boats are? Riko tries it. Excuse me. Do you know where the nearest station is? Say it with me. Do you know where the nearest station is? Excellent! Another polite way is, Could you tell me where the station is? Mr. Lee says, Of course! It's Clock Tower Station. It's a five-minute walk. He draws a little map for us. Let's read Mr. Lee's map card. "From the Seagull Hotel to Clock Tower Station. Go out of the front entrance and turn left. Walk straight along Harbor Street for two blocks. You will see a bakery on the corner. Turn right at the bakery. The station is at the end of that street, right next to the tall clock tower. You can't miss it! It takes about five minutes on foot." Which way do we turn at the entrance? Left. Where is the station? Next to the clock tower. Kiko asks, Could you tell me when the next train to the harbor leaves? Mr. Lee checks and says, At nine thirty. I say, Thank you! Stay close to me, everyone. Now, phonics. Tomorrow has one m and two r's. Different has two f's. D, i, f, f, e, r, e, n, t. Arrive has two r's. Next time, we will ask Mr. Lee about a good place to eat dinner!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Do you know where the nearest station is? We spent the day at the harbor, and now we are very hungry! Birimo's tummy rumbles like a little thunderstorm. I say, Let's ask Mr. Lee. He knows the city very well. When you want a good idea from someone who knows a place, you can say, Could you recommend a good restaurant? To recommend something means to say, This one is good. You should try it! Haru tries it. Excuse me. Could you recommend a good restaurant? Say it with me. Could you recommend a good restaurant? Great! Mr. Lee smiles and asks, What kind of food do you like? Riko says, We love fish! Mr. Lee says, Then how about the River Fish Restaurant? It's right by the river. He gives us a page from the hotel's city guide. Let's read the guide. "River Fish Restaurant. This small family restaurant sits right by the river, near the old stone bridge. The fish comes fresh from the harbor every morning. Try the grilled fish with lemon, or the famous fish soup. There is a children's menu with fish and chips and fruit juice. It is open from eleven in the morning to nine at night. Ask for a table by the window and watch the boats go by!" Where is the restaurant? By the river. What time does it open? At eleven in the morning. Kiko says, Thank you for the great idea, Mr. Lee! Mr. Lee says, My pleasure. I'm sure you'll love it. We decide to go there another day. Now, phonics. Recommend has one c and two m's. Excellent has two l's. Suggest has two g's. S, u, g, g, e, s, t. To suggest means to give an idea, like, I suggest the fish soup! Next time, we will practice all our hotel English, and we will need umbrellas!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Could you recommend a good restaurant? Today, we are practicing all our hotel English. Birimo says, I'm playing Mr. Lee! Welcome to the Seagull Hotel! We take turns. Haru checks in with his reservation. Riko asks for an extra pillow. Kiko asks where the nearest station is. Then, oh no! Dark clouds are rolling in, and it starts to rain. We want to walk to the River Market, but we don't have umbrellas. I say, Many hotels lend umbrellas to guests. Let's ask politely. Kiko goes to the front desk with me and says, I'd like to borrow an umbrella. Could you lend me one? Say it with me. I'd like to borrow an umbrella. Could you lend me one? Super! Borrow means you take something and give it back later. Lend means you give something, and it comes back to you. Mr. Lee points to a sign. Let's read the sign. "Rainy Day? We can help! Seagull Hotel guests may borrow umbrellas from the front desk for free. Large umbrellas are blue, and small umbrellas for children are yellow. Please write your room number on the list when you borrow one. If you need a raincoat, just ask. Bring the umbrellas back to the front desk before you check out. Enjoy Brightwater, rain or shine!" What color are the children's umbrellas? Yellow. When do we bring them back? Before we check out. Then Skye lands by the door, shaking rain from her wings. She says, Every trip is a story, and today's story is about kind words! She opens the Wing Stamp Book and presses our third stamp onto the page. Now, phonics. Let's review. Accommodation has two c's and two m's. Recommend has one c and two m's. Visitor. Vis means see. Gate 41C is gate forty-one C, not fourteen C. Next time, I will tell you a surprising secret about my suitcase!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I'd like to borrow an umbrella. Could you lend me one? This morning, I sit down with you in the lobby. I say, I have something to tell you. On the day we arrived, my suitcase didn't come out at baggage claim. I didn't want you to worry on our special day, so I used my backpack. Haru says, Oh! That's why you wore the same green sweater every day! I laugh and say, Today, let's go to the Baggage Service desk at Brightwater Airport together. When your bag doesn't come, don't get upset. Just explain clearly and politely. My suitcase didn't arrive. Say it with me. My suitcase didn't arrive. Good! At the airport, a kind woman at the desk listens carefully. She asks, What does it look like? I say, It's big and blue, with a yellow ribbon on the handle. It has a name tag, too. The woman says, We're very sorry. Could you fill out this form, please? Let's read the form. "Baggage Service Form. Flight: 1120 from Skyport. Item: one large suitcase. Color: blue. Special marks: a yellow ribbon on the handle and a name tag. Inside: clothes, shoes, a hairbrush, and a travel guide. Please send the bag to the Seagull Hotel in Brightwater. We apologize for the trouble. We will call your hotel as soon as we find your bag." What color is the suitcase? Blue. What is on the handle? A yellow ribbon. That night, the phone in our room rings. Mr. Lee says, Good news! Your suitcase is here at the front desk! We all cheer. Now, phonics. Today's words end in ize, and they are all verbs. Apology, drop the y, add ize. Apologize. Real, add ize. Realize means suddenly know that something is true. Summary, drop the y, add ize. Summarize means tell the main points. Next time, our room gets very hot, and something is broken!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, My suitcase didn't arrive. Good news! I have my blue suitcase back. But today is the hottest day of our trip. After lunch, we come back to Room 512 to rest. Phew! It's like an oven in here! Riko presses the button on the remote control. The air conditioner makes a strange rattling noise, and only warm air comes out. I say, Let's call the front desk. Riko, would you like to try? I'll be right next to you. To explain a problem politely, start with I'm afraid. I'm afraid（ざんねんですが）makes your words soft and kind. Riko picks up the room phone and says, Hello, this is Room 512. I'm afraid the air conditioner is broken. Say it with me. I'm afraid the air conditioner is broken. Perfect! Riko adds, It's making a strange noise, and it's still hot. Mr. Lee says, I'm so sorry. We'll send someone right away. While we wait, Kiko finds a card next to the TV. Let's read the card. "How to Use Your Air Conditioner. Press the red button to turn it on or off. Use the up and down arrows to make the room warmer or cooler. Keep the windows closed when it is on. If the air conditioner does not work, please do not try to fix it yourself. Call the front desk, and a member of our repair team will come to help you." What does the red button do? It turns the air conditioner on or off. What should you do if it doesn't work? Call the front desk. Soon, Sam the repair person arrives with his toolbox. Birimo says, I'm playing his helper! and holds the flashlight. Now, phonics. More ize verbs! Modern, add ize. Modernize means make something new. Energy, drop the y, add ize. Energize means give energy. Final, add ize. Finalize means finish the last details. Next time, Sam has some news, and we need a new plan!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I'm afraid the air conditioner is broken. Sam looks inside the air conditioner for a long time. Then he shakes his head. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Could you give us a different room instead? We love our new room. But this morning, I'm looking through my backpack. Then my jacket. Then my suitcase. I say calmly, Everyone, I can't find my passport. Your passports are safe in the travel pouch, but mine isn't there. Then she adds, Don't worry. When something is lost, the first thing to do is stay calm. If you ever lose something important on a trip, tell an adult right away. I'm the adult, so I'll ask at the front desk. I lost my passport. What should I do? Say it with me. I lost my passport. What should I do? Well done! We check all our bags together, and then we all go down to the lobby. Mr. Lee listens kindly and asks, Where did you last use it? I remember. At the Baggage Service desk at the airport! I showed it there for the form. Mr. Lee says, I'll call the airport for you. While he calls, he gives us a card. Let's read the card. "Lost Your Passport? Don't panic. First, look carefully in your bags and pockets. Next, think about the last place you used it. Then, tell the hotel front desk. We can make phone calls for you. If you still cannot find it, an adult should go to the police and then contact their country's embassy. Children, always keep your passport with a grown-up you trust." Who should go to the embassy? An adult. Who should children keep their passports with? A grown-up they trust. Good news! The airport has it. It's safe at the Baggage Service desk. We all go to the airport together and pick it up. Now, phonics. Memory, drop the y, add ize. Memorize. Sympathy, drop the y, add ize. Sympathize means understand how someone feels. Symbol, add ize. Symbolize. Next time, we will say a big thank you to everyone who helped us!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I lost my passport. What should I do? My passport is back, safe in the travel pouch with ours. We had a late suitcase, a broken air conditioner, and a missing passport. But every problem was solved, because we stayed calm and polite, and kind people helped us. Today, we are making thank-you cards. When someone helps you, you can say, Thank you for your help. And to make it extra warm, add, That's very kind of you. Say it with me. Thank you for your help. That's very kind of you. Beautiful! First, we play Problem Solved! Birimo says, I'm playing Mr. Lee! Haru says, I'm afraid the shower is broken. Birimo answers, I'm so sorry. We'll fix it right away. Riko says, Could we have a different room instead? Then Kiko reads her card to the real Mr. Lee. Let's read Kiko's card. "Dear Mr. Lee, thank you for your help this week. You gave us a cool new room with a view of the Clock Tower, and you called the airport to find Ms. Emma's passport. You always smile, even when there is a problem. That's very kind of you. We will never forget the Seagull Hotel. Love, Kiko, Haru, Riko, and Birimo." What can we see from our new room? The Clock Tower. Who did Mr. Lee call? The airport. We also make a card for the Baggage Service staff. Then, at twelve thirty, Skye flies in through the lobby door. She says, Every trip is a story, and this one has a happy ending! She gives us our fourth stamp. Now, phonics. Let's review. Apology, drop the y, add ize. Apologize. Real, add ize. Realize. Luggage has two g's. L, u, g, g, a, g, e. Vision. Vis means see, so vision is how well you can see. 12:30 is twelve thirty. Next time, we will explore Brightwater and ask someone to take our picture!

phonics.tipJa: イギリスと アメリカで ちがう ことばが あるよ。underground（イギリス）＝ subway（アメリカ）ちかてつ。sidewalk（アメリカ）＝ pavement（イギリス）ほどう。queue（イギリス）＝ line（アメリカ）れつ。q-u-e-u-e と 書いて「キュー」と よむよ。timetable（イギリス）＝ schedule（アメリカ）じこくひょう。どちらも ただしい 英語！

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Thank you for your help. That's very kind of you. Today, it's time to explore Brightwater! The sun is shining after yesterday's rain. We walk along the river, and Skye flies above us in her blue scarf. She calls down, Every trip is a story! Soon we reach Clock Tower Square. The tall Clock Tower stands in the middle, next to a fountain and a statue of a seagull. We want a picture of all of us together. I smile at a kind woman with a map and say, Excuse me. Could you take our picture? The woman says, Of course! Say it with me. Excuse me. Could you take our picture? Great! Remember, always ask with a grown-up right next to you. Let's read the sign in the square. "Welcome to Clock Tower Square. The Clock Tower was built more than two hundred years ago. Its bell rings every hour, from eight in the morning to eight at night. Please stay on the sidewalk and do not climb into the fountain. The subway station is across the bridge. Please wait in line at the ticket machines and check the schedule on the wall." When does the bell ring? Every hour, from eight in the morning to eight at night. Where is the subway station? Across the bridge. Just then, the bell rings. Bong, bong, bong! Click! The woman takes our picture at the perfect moment. Now, phonics. Today, we learn British and American words. Underground. In the UK, people say underground. In the US, people say subway. Sidewalk. In the US, people say sidewalk. In the UK, people say pavement. Queue. Q, u, e, u, e. It sounds just like the letter Q! In the US, people say line. Timetable. In the US, people say schedule. Both are correct English. Next time, we will go to the fish restaurant by the river and order lunch!

vocab.ja: ウェイター（お店の 人）

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Excuse me. Could you take our picture? Today, we're hungry after our long walk. We go to the fish restaurant by the river. Mr. Lee recommended it, remember? We sit at a table by the window, and we can see boats on the water. A friendly waiter comes over with glasses of water and says, Good afternoon! Riko smiles and asks, Could we have the menu, please? Say it with me. Could we have the menu, please? Great! We say we, because we are a group. Let's read the menu. "River Fish Restaurant. Today's Lunch. Fish and chips with peas, ten dollars. Grilled salmon with rice and salad, twelve dollars. Fish soup with warm bread, eight dollars. Children's plate, small fish and chips with apple juice, six dollars. Desserts. Chocolate cake, four dollars. Ice cream, three dollars. Every children's plate comes with a free cookie. Please tell our staff if you have any allergies." How much is the fish soup? Eight dollars. What comes with every children's plate? A free cookie. The waiter asks, What would you like? Haru says, I'd like the fish and chips, please. Birimo tries to order three ice creams, and I laugh. One is enough, Birimo! After lunch, I ask, Could we have the check, please? Now, phonics. Today, let's learn more British and American words. Bill. In the UK, people say bill. In the US, people say check. Biscuit. In the UK, a biscuit is a sweet, flat snack. In the US, people call it a cookie. Candy. In the US, people say candy. In the UK, people say sweets. Trash. In the US, people say trash. In the UK, people say rubbish. Both are correct English. Next time, we will meet two friendly travelers at the hotel, one from the UK and one from the US!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Could we have the menu, please? After lunch, we stop by the Seagull Hotel. Two friendly travelers are drinking tea in the lobby. Mrs. Brown is from the UK, and Mr. Green is from the US. They are on a trip, too! Mrs. Brown says, I'm on holiday with my sister. Mr. Green laughs and says, And I'm on vacation with my son. When it's time to go upstairs, Mrs. Brown says, Let's take the lift. Mr. Green says, You mean the elevator! Everyone laughs. I explain, English is spoken in many countries, and some words are different. In the UK, people say lift. Say it with me. In the UK, people say lift. Great! In the US, people say elevator. Both are correct English. Mrs. Brown shows us a little card she made for her grandson. Let's read the card. "Words from Two Countries. In the UK, we take the lift up to our room. In the US, people take the elevator. In the UK, we go on holiday in the summer. In the US, people go on vacation. We often eat biscuits with our tea, and in the US, people often eat cookies with milk. We use different words, but we can always understand each other with a smile." What do people in the US often eat with milk? Cookies. How can we always understand each other? With a smile. Birimo says, In Birimo Land, people say up box! Mr. Green laughs so hard that he almost drops his cup. Now, phonics. Today, let's compare four words. Lift and elevator. In the UK, people say lift. In the US, people say elevator. Elevator has a strong first part. EL, e, va, tor. Holiday and vacation. In the UK, people say holiday. In the US, people say vacation. Vacation has a strong middle part. Va, CA, tion. Next time, we will go to the City Museum and buy tickets for everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, In the UK, people say lift. Today, we visit the City Museum. It's a big stone building near the castle hill, and there's a dinosaur skeleton in the front window! First, we go to the ticket office. I look at the price list and count. We are one adult and four children: Haru, Riko, Kiko, and Birimo. I say to the staff member, One adult and four children, please. Is there a family discount? Say it with me. One adult and four children, please. Is there a family discount? Great! A discount makes the price lower. Let's read the price list. "City Museum Tickets. Adults, twelve dollars. Children aged six to twelve, six dollars. Children under six, free. Family ticket, for up to two adults and four children visiting together, thirty dollars. Open every day from nine thirty to five. Don't miss the Color Room and the Science Center on the second floor! The Little Theater shows a puppet play at two o'clock." How much is a family ticket? Thirty dollars. What time is the puppet play? At two o'clock. Birimo whispers, Do creatures need tickets, too? The staff member smiles and says, Friends of all kinds are welcome, and you count as a child! So the family ticket is perfect for us, and it's cheaper, too. Now, phonics. Today, let's look at spelling. Colour. In the UK, colour has a u. In the US, it's c, o, l, o, r. Centre. In the UK, centre ends with r, e. In the US, center ends with e, r. Theatre. It's the same pattern! In the UK, it ends with r, e. In the US, it ends with e, r. Favourite. In the UK, favourite has a u, too. The sounds are almost the same. Next time, we will tell Skye all about our wonderful day in the city!

phonics.tipJa: まとめ。lift（イギリスの エレベーター。アメリカは elevator）、colour（イギリスは u が ある。アメリカは color）、memorize（memory の y を とって ＋ ize → おぼえる）、necessary（c は 1つ、s は 2つ）、Flight 760（seven sixty。2けたずつ よむ）。

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, One adult and four children, please. Is there a family discount? Tonight, Skye flies down to the hotel garden. She wants to hear all about our day in Brightwater. I say, Let's tell the story in order. First, then, after that, and finally. Haru starts. We visited the Clock Tower. Then, we took a boat on the river. Say it with me. We visited the Clock Tower. Then, we took a boat on the river. Great! Visited and took tell Skye that it happened in the past. Skye wrote about her day in her notebook, too. Let's read Skye's notebook. "My Day in Brightwater. This morning, I flew over the Clock Tower and said hello to the seagulls. Then, I rested on top of the old castle. After that, I watched my friends on a river boat. They waved at me, and I waved my wing back! In the afternoon, I followed them to the City Museum. Finally, I watched a beautiful sunset over the harbor. Every trip is a story!" Where did Skye rest? On top of the old castle. Where did she watch the sunset? Over the harbor. Then Skye opens the Wing Stamp Book and says, You told your story so well! Here is your fifth stamp. Stamp! It shows a little clock tower. Only one page is empty now. Now, phonics. Let's review. Lift. In the UK, people say lift. In the US, people say elevator. Colour. In the UK, colour has a u. Memorize. Memory, drop the y, and add i, z, e. Necessary. One c and two s's. Flight 760. Read it in two parts. Flight seven sixty. Mrs. Brown is flying home on Flight 760 tomorrow, so we memorize the number and wish her a good trip. Next time, we will write an email to the hotel front desk to ask about the airport bus.

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, We visited the Clock Tower. Then, we took a boat on the river. Our trip is almost over. On our last day, we need to get to Brightwater Airport. Is there an airport bus? I say, Let's write an email to the front desk together. I'll send it from the hotel computer in the lobby. An email to a hotel starts with Dear, and then we say why we are writing. I'm writing to ask about the airport bus. Say it with me. I'm writing to ask about the airport bus. Great! Let's read our email. "Dear Front Desk, I'm writing to ask about the airport bus. Our group of five is leaving on Saturday morning, and our flight leaves at ten thirty. Could you tell me what time the bus leaves the hotel? Is it necessary to book seats? We also have five suitcases. Thank you for a wonderful stay at the Seagull Hotel. We look forward to hearing from you. Best wishes, Ms. Emma and friends, Room 507" What day is our group leaving? Saturday morning. How many suitcases do we have? Five. Kiko asks, Should we write our home address, too? I say, No, we don't need to. Our room number is enough. An hour later, Mr. Lee replies. The airport bus leaves from the front door at seven fifteen, and seats are free for hotel guests. Birimo says, Mr. Lee writes emails with a smile, too! Now, phonics. Let's review. Seat 32F. Read it seat thirty-two F. Supervise. Super means over, and vis means see. When you supervise, you watch people and make sure they are safe. Address. Two d's and two s's. A, d, d, r, e, s, s. Finalize. Final plus ize. We finalize our plans for the last day. Holiday. In the UK, people say holiday. In the US, people say vacation. Next time, we will read a travel brochure and choose a tour for our last afternoon!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I'm writing to ask about the airport bus. Today is our last full day in Brightwater, and we have one free afternoon. Mr. Lee gives us a bright brochure from the front desk. It shows three tours for visitors. I say, We can only choose one, so let's read carefully. Read the brochure. Which tour would you choose? Say it with me. Read the brochure. Which tour would you choose? Great! Let's read the brochure together. "Brightwater Afternoon Tours. River Boat Tour. Ride a boat under five old bridges and see the city from the water. One hour. Castle Walk. Walk up the hill with a tour guide and enjoy the best viewpoint in town. About two hours. Wear good shoes! Market Food Tour. Taste fresh fruit, warm bread, and fish soup at the River Market food stalls. Ninety minutes. All tours start at one o'clock in front of the Old Theater. Children must come with an adult." Which tour is the longest? The Castle Walk. Where do all the tours start? In front of the Old Theater. Kiko says, I'd choose the River Boat Tour because I love boats. Haru wants the Castle Walk because he loves castles. Birimo wants the Market Food Tour, of course! We already took a boat yesterday, so we vote. The Castle Walk wins, and I promise Birimo a snack at the top. Now, phonics. Let's review. Gate 102. Read it gate one oh two. Zero is oh. Visitor. Visit means go and see, and or means a person. Excellent. Two l's, and it ends with e, n, t. Modernize. Modern plus ize. The Old Theater was modernized last year, so it looks new inside. Theatre. In the UK, theatre ends with r, e. In the US, people write theater. Next time, we will write our own travel journals about this trip!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Read the brochure. Which tour would you choose? Tonight is our last night in Brightwater. I give each of you a small notebook. I say, A travel journal helps you remember your trip forever. Write what you did, and then write your favorite part. Riko writes first. On the first day, we visited the market. The best part was the boat ride. Say it with me. On the first day, we visited the market. The best part was the boat ride. Great! Kiko glues her museum ticket on her page, and Haru draws the Clock Tower. Let's read Riko's journal. "My Travel Journal. On the first day, we visited the River Market. I tried a sweet orange from a food stall. On the second day, we went to the City Museum. I was surprised by the giant dinosaur. The best part was the boat ride on the river, because Skye flew right next to our boat. Tomorrow, the airport bus leaves at seven fifteen in the morning. Now I realize that polite words really open doors!" What surprised Riko at the museum? The giant dinosaur. Why was the boat ride the best part? Because Skye flew next to the boat. Birimo writes only one line. The best part was all the food. Everyone laughs. Now, phonics. Let's review. Seven fifteen. Fifteen has a strong end. Fifteen, not fifty. Visit. Vis means see. When you visit, you go and see a place or a person. Tomorrow. One m and two r's. T, o, m, o, r, r, o, w. Realize. Real plus ize. It means to suddenly understand something. Favourite. In the UK, favourite has a u. In the US, people write favorite. Next time, we will go back to the airport and use all our polite requests one more time!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, On the first day, we visited the market. The best part was the boat ride. This morning, we take the airport bus at seven fifteen and say goodbye to Mr. Lee. He waves from the front door with a big smile. Now we are back at Brightwater Airport. It's very busy, and we can't see the check-in counters. I keep everyone close and stop a friendly staff member. I say, Excuse me. Would you mind helping us? Do you know where the check-in counter is? Say it with me. Would you mind helping us? Do you know where the check-in counter is? Great! That's two polite requests in a row. The staff member says, Not at all. It's next to the gift shop. Let's read the departures board. "Brightwater Airport Departures. Flight 318 to Skyport, ten thirty, gate 6, on time. Flight 452 to Seashell Bay, ten fifty, gate 9, delayed. Flight 117 to Coral Island, eleven twenty, gate 3, on time. Please check in at least two hours before your flight. Have your passport and boarding pass ready. Thank you for visiting Brightwater. Please come back soon!" What time does Flight 318 leave? At ten thirty. Which flight is delayed? Flight 452. At the counter, Kiko asks, Could I have a window seat, please? The clerk says, Certainly. Then we buy souvenirs at the gift shop. Haru chooses a Clock Tower keychain, and Riko buys a postcard for Skye. Now, phonics. Let's review. Flight 318. Read it flight three eighteen. Visa. Vis means see. A visa is a paper that lets you enter a country. Luggage. Two g's, and it ends with a, g, e. Apologize. Apology, drop the y, and add i, z, e. Elevator. In the US, people say elevator. In the UK, people say lift. Next time, we will fly home to the Airport of Wings for our big Travel Talk Show!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Would you mind helping us? Do you know where the check-in counter is? We're back! Our plane landed at the Airport of Wings, and today we're on the observation deck. Visibility is perfect, so we can see the white wing roof and the blue sea. It's time for the World 34 Travel Talk Show! Haru holds the microphone and tells the story of Flight 205. Riko talks about the City Museum, and Kiko shows her travel journal. Birimo shows everyone his Clock Tower keychain. Then I say, We learned so many polite words on this trip. Traveling is the best way to learn! Say it with me. Traveling is the best way to learn! Wonderful! Suddenly, Skye lands on the railing with a letter in her beak. Let's read the letter. "Dear friends of the Airport of Wings, Congratulations on finishing your trip! You asked politely, solved problems calmly, and thanked everyone you met. Now, children from many places are going to meet at the Hall of Wisdom. They will share ideas and talk together about our world. We would love you to join us. Please come with your teacher. Your new friends are waiting!" Where will the children meet? At the Hall of Wisdom. Who should come with the friends? Their teacher. Skye smiles and says, Congratulations! Here is your sixth stamp! Stamp! Then something amazing happens. The six stamps make a picture of a big building with a round roof. That's the Hall of Wisdom! Now, phonics. Let's review. Flight 205. Read it flight two oh five. Visibility. Visible means you can see it, so visibility means how far you can see. Recommend. One c and two m's. Memorize. Memory, drop the y, and add i, z, e. Vacation. In the US, people say vacation. In the UK, people say holiday. Goodbye, Skye! Thank you, Airport of Wings! See you at the Hall of Wisdom!

aiTask.goalJa: AI の スカイに たびの かんそうを きかれたら Traveling is the best way to learn! を つかって こたえよう。たびで いちばん やくに たった ていねいな たのみかたも 1つ 言おう
aiTask.starterEn: Let's pretend I'm Skye. Every trip is a story! Welcome home to the Airport of Wings! What was your favorite part of the trip? What did you learn?

segments.say: Welcome home, everyone! Last time, we asked, Would you mind helping us? Now we've landed at the Airport of Wings. What a view from here!

segments.subtitleEn: Welcome home, everyone! Last time, we asked, Would you mind helping us? Now we've landed at the Airport of Wings. What a view from here!
